Real defect, confirmed: the worked side-pot example in Part 6.3 has a genuine arithmetic error — the 'Level 200' pot layer is computed as (200-100)*2 and written down as 100, when (200-100)*2 = 200. summary: The candidate is broad and largely complete, covering every major area the reference does and adding useful extras (an invariant list, a testing checklist, inline API/CORS detail). Its most serious real defects are self-inflicted, not comparative: a leftover 'let me rethink' draft fragment left inside a safety-critical function, and a worked side-pot example whose own arithmetic is wrong and self-contradicts the document's own stated chip-conservation invariant. The turn-enforcement-ordering complaint that originally also docked this candidate does not hold up — the reference document it was checked against turned out to have stale content contradicting the real system's actual behavior, now fixed. Net: a solidly complete design let down by two real, verifiable internal-consistency slips rather than by any comparative shortfall against the reference.
